editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.18, where the opening statement defines finite limits and colimits through finiteness of their indexing categories; its duality statements distinguish the two constructions.

definitions.text: A limit of a diagram F:I→C is a finite limit if the indexing category I has finitely many objects and finitely many morphisms, including identities.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: finite limit

definitions.text: A colimit of a diagram F:I→C is a finite colimit when the index category I contains only finitely many objects and morphisms.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: finite colimit

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 4.15, which explicitly constructs limits of sets as compatible tuples in a product and colimits as an equivalence-class quotient of the disjoint union. These provide distinct concrete formulations.

definitions.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its limit is the subset of the Cartesian product ∏_i F(i) consisting of families (x_i) satisfying F(u)(x_i)=x_j for every arrow u:i→j in I.
definitions.source_section: Section 4.15 explicit formula for limit in Sets
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: inverse limit of a diagram of sets

definitions.text: For a set-valued diagram F:I→Sets, its colimit is the disjoint union of the sets F(i), modulo the equivalence relation generated by x∼F(u)(x) for each arrow u:i→j.
definitions.source_section: Section 4.15 explicit formula for colimit in Sets
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: colimit of a diagram of sets

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Fields 9.28, entitled Review but containing Definition 9.28.1. It explicitly separates algebraic, separable algebraic, purely inseparable, normal and Galois field extensions, so the chapter heading cannot justify treating it as definition-free.

definitions.text: An extension K/k of fields is algebraic if every element α∈K satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in k.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: algebraic field extension

definitions.text: An algebraic extension K/k is separable if the minimal polynomial of each α∈K has no repeated roots over an algebraic closure of k.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: separable algebraic extension

definitions.text: An algebraic field extension K/k in characteristic p>0 is purely inseparable if every α∈K has α^(p^n)∈k for some integer n≥0.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: purely inseparable extension

definitions.text: An algebraic extension K/k is normal if every irreducible polynomial over k having one root in K splits completely into linear factors over K.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: normal algebraic extension

definitions.text: An algebraic extension K/k is Galois precisely when it is both separable and normal over k.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: Galois field extension

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.40, Definition 4.40.1, which requires equivalence over the base category to a slice category C/X, not strict equality or just an isomorphism class of presheaves.

definitions.text: A category p:S→C fibred in groupoids is representable if there exists an object X of C and an equivalence over C between S and the slice category C/X.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: representable category fibred in groupoids

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.32 Definition 4.32.1. This describes the 2-category Cat/C of categories over C, including 1-morphisms commuting strictly with projections and 2-morphisms covering identities.

definitions.text: For a category C, its 2-category of categories over C has as objects functors p:S→C, as 1-morphisms functors G:S→S′ satisfying p′G=p, and as 2-morphisms natural transformations between such functors whose components project to identity morphisms in C.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: 2-category of categories over a base category

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Schemes 26.15, Definition 26.15.1, which defines representability of a contravariant set-valued functor on schemes by the functor of points of a scheme, notwithstanding the section heading's emphasis on a criterion.

definitions.text: A contravariant functor F:Sch^op→Sets is representable by a scheme if some scheme X admits a natural isomorphism F(T)≅Hom_Sch(T,X) for every scheme T.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: functor representable by a scheme

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.42, Definition 10.42.1. The source distinguishes separably generated extensions, admitting a suitably separable transcendence basis, from the stronger condition that all finitely generated intermediate extensions are separably generated.

definitions.text: A field extension K/k is separably generated if there exists a transcendence basis B⊆K over k such that K is a separable algebraic extension of the rational-function field k(B).
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: separably generated extension

definitions.text: An arbitrary field extension K/k is separable if every finitely generated intermediate extension E/k with k⊆E⊆K is separably generated.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: separable extension not necessarily algebraic

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.130 and Lemma 10.130.1. It identifies the Cohen–Macaulay locus of a finite-type k-algebra as the primes where the localized algebra is Cohen–Macaulay, and proves the openness of that locus in the stated setting.

definitions.text: For a Noetherian ring S, the Cohen–Macaulay locus of Spec(S) is the set of prime ideals q for which the local ring S_q is Cohen–Macaulay.
definitions.source_section: Section 10.130, locus used in Lemma 10.130.1 and openness discussion
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Cohen–Macaulay locus of the spectrum

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.149 and Lemma 10.149.1, giving the universal square-zero thickening associated with a formally unramified ring map. This is a specific universal lifting construction, not just the adjective 'thickening'.

definitions.text: For a formally unramified ring map R→S, a universal square-zero thickening is a surjective R-algebra map S′→S with square-zero kernel such that every R-algebra map S→A/I, for any square-zero ideal I of A, has a unique compatible lift S′→A.
definitions.context_hint: Deformation theory: universal first-order thickening of a formally unramified map

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 4.35 Definition 4.35.1. A functor p:S→C is fibred in groupoids if arrows into base objects can be lifted and if all relevant lift comparison arrows exist uniquely, so vertical fibres are groupoids.

definitions.text: A functor p:E→C is a category fibred in groupoids if every morphism f:V→U in C lifts to a morphism y→x above f for each object x over U, and each compatible base morphism between the sources of two arrows into x lifts uniquely to a morphism between their domains.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: category fibred in groupoids

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.118, Generic flatness. The main lemmas assert that finite-type algebras and finite modules over Noetherian domains become flat or free after inverting a nonzero base element. This is an existence theorem, not a new independent object with the name 'generic flatness'.

Read Stacks Schemes 26.20 Definition 26.20.1 and the subsequent valuative criterion. The source defines universal closedness via closedness after every base change; this must not be confused with the additional properties defining properness.

definitions.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S is universally closed if for every morphism S′→S the induced base-change map X×_S S′→S′ sends closed subsets to closed subsets.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: universally closed scheme morphism

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.27, examples of spectra of rings. This section explicitly works through examples of prime spectra of quotient rings and their induced maps; no new generic mathematical concept called 'examples of spectra' is defined.

Read Stacks 10.154, which introduces filtered colimits of étale R-algebras as an object of study and proves stability under base changes and composition. The corresponding property is described precisely without treating the result itself as a definition.

definitions.text: An R-algebra A is a filtered colimit of étale R-algebras if there exists a filtered diagram of étale R-algebras (A_i) and an R-algebra isomorphism A≅colim_i A_i.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: filtered colimit of étale ring maps

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.22 Lemma 10.22.1. It provides an equivalent characterization of closed unions of connected components in affine spectra through ideals generated by idempotents.

definitions.text: A subset T of Spec(R) is closed and a union of connected components if and only if it can be expressed as V(I) for an ideal I generated by idempotent elements of R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: closed unions of connected components of Spec(R)

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.20, Nakayama's lemma. The source proves multiple forms of the module-generation and vanishing theorem using the Jacobson radical. It does not introduce a new named mathematical object called 'Nakayama's lemma'; the underlying definitions of Jacobson radical, finite module, and local ring require their own source citations.
